q: A footing buried 600mm below grade may project how far toward a public sidewalk?
ref: IRR Rule X, §1002(c) — Projection into Alleys or Streets
n: “Foundations may be permitted to encroach into public sidewalk areas to a width not exceeding 500 millimeters; provided, that the top of the said foundations is not less than 600 millimeters below the established grade.” Note the separate rule for footings along a national road (2.40m deep): those may only project 300mm.

q: What is the least height allowed for the fence around a construction or demolition site?
ref: IRR Rule XI, §1106(c) — Pedestrian Protection, Fences
n: “Fences shall be built of an approved material, not less than 2.40 meters in height above grade, and be placed on the side of the walkway nearest to the building site. Fences shall enclose entirely the building site.”

q: Where the distance from the outermost face of the building to the inner edge of the sidewalk equals the building height, what is required?
o: A fence, a canopy, and a net
A fence and a temporary walkway
n: Only a fence is required because the setback is already more than half of the building height — the threshold at which canopies and nets start being triggered under Table 1106-A.

q: Using the occupant load factors in Rule 12, what is the least floor area for a classroom holding 30 students and one teacher?
ref: IRR Rule XII, §1207 — Occupant Load Factors (Educational)
n: 31 persons × 1.80 sqm/person (classroom occupant load factor) = 55.80 sqm.

q: Under Rule 12, what is the occupant load factor for hotels?
ref: IRR Rule XII, §1207 — Occupant Load Factors (Residential)
n: Hotels, apartment buildings, and lodging or rooming houses are factored at 18.60 sqm/person. 28.00 sqm/person is the figure for detached single and two-family dwellings instead.

q: A floor carrying an occupant load of 700 requires at least how many exits?
ref: IRR Rule XII, §1210 — Number of Exits
n: “Every storey or portion thereof, having an occupant load of 500 to 999 shall have at least three (3) exits.” Four exits only kick in at 1,000 or more.

q: Where a building has an automatic fire extinguishing system, how far may the travel distance to an exit reach?
ref: IRR Rule XII, §1210 — Distance to Exits
n: “No point in a building without a sprinkler system shall be more than 45.00 meters from an exit... In a building equipped with a complete automatic fire extinguishing system the distance from exits may be increased to 60.00 meters.”

q: What is the least door height the Building Code allows?
n: The general minimum door height under PD 1096 is 2.00 meters, applied consistently across occupancy types.

q: For an occupant load of 15, what stair width is required at least?
n: Stairs are tiered by occupant load: under 10 occupants → 750mm; 10 to 50 occupants → 900mm; more than 50 → 1,100mm. An occupant load of 15 falls in the 900mm tier.

q: At what height must handrails be mounted under the Building Code?
n: Handrails on stairs are required to be mounted between 800mm and 900mm above the nosing of the treads.

q: What is the least depth allowed for an elevator pit?
n: The minimum depth of a hoistway pit, measured from the underside of the elevator car, is 600mm.

q: How many seats at most may sit between two aisles?
n: “The maximum number of seats in any row extending from one aisle to another shall be fourteen.” This may only be increased to 30 under specific conditions on exit width and seat spacing.

q: What least thickness is required for a glass panel measuring 2.50 x 2.50 m?
ref: IRR Rule XVIII, §1801 — Glass and Glazing
n: For an exterior-grade panel of this size (6.25 sqm), 12mm is the standard minimum used to keep deflection and breaking-stress levels within safe limits for an unsupported span this large.

q: What is the greatest width allowed for a door leaf?
o: There is no maximum width for a door leaf
n: Remember: while there is no maximum width for the doorway or the door opening, each door leaf or door panel can only be 1200mm long at the most — so the doorway itself has no cap, but each individual leaf does.

q: How many seats at most may sit between a wall and an aisle?
n: “The maximum number of seats in any row extending from one aisle to a wall shall be seven” — exactly half the 14-seat limit that applies between two aisles.
